subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this Gateway control-plane and per-agent runtime split as a core architecture track, and what is the first supported milestone?
rationale: The next step requires choosing public protocol, config, lifecycle, security, migration, and deployment boundaries that automation cannot safely decide from source inspection alone.

options.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines the local-split protocol, trust model, session ownership, and per-agent lifecycle before container or Kubernetes runners.

options.title: Narrow To Execution Placement
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82017 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84758 as the current scope and defer the broader Gateway/control-plane split until placement contracts are reviewed.

options.title: Defer Core Architecture Change
options.body: Keep supporting separate-gateway and operator workarounds while declining a first-class distributed runtime boundary for now.

recommendation.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines the local-split protocol, trust model, session ownership, and per-agent lifecycle before container or Kubernetes runners.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest architecture-review signal from related runtime-isolation, scaling, and security-boundary work.
